title: Continuous coefficient endomorphisms, the rank-one corner, and the normalized derived projection
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a nonarchimedean normed extension field $F/E$ whose norm restricts to that of $E$. Put $A(P)=C(P,E)$ and $B(P)=C(P,F)$ on profinite sets, with ALL continuous functions, and let $A\to B$ be induced by inclusion [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. For every scheme $Z$ put $A_Z=p_Z^*A$, $B_Z=p_Z^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules, ordinary unbounded derived categories, exact scalar restriction $r_Z$, and $T_Z=B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}-$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_X})$, with $M=Rf_{*,A}K$ and $N=Rf_{*,B}T_XK$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Define $\beta_{f,K}:T_YM\to N$ as the geometric-adjunction transpose of $f_B^*T_YM\cong T_Xf_A^*M\xrightarrow{T_X\varepsilon}T_XK$, using the canonical balanced tensor comparison [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization].

Let $D=\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{cts}}_E(F)$, the unital $E$-algebra of continuous $E$-linear endomorphisms, with composition as multiplication. Fix a continuous $E$-linear $\lambda:F\to E$ satisfying $\lambda(1)=1$. Set $e(w)=\lambda(w)1$ and $\theta_v(w)=\lambda(w)v$ for $v,w\in F$.

There is a canonical adjunction-compatible comparison $\sigma:r_YN\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,A}r_XT_XK$. Through $\sigma$, postcomposition by $d\in D$ on $B$, tensoring with $K$, and applying $Rf_{*,A}$ give a unital $E$-algebra action $\rho:D\to\operatorname{End}_{D(A_Y)}(r_YN)$. For $v\in F$, $\rho(m_v)$ is the underlying action of the constant scalar $v$ on $N$, where $m_v(w)=vw$.

The derived scalar unit $\eta_K:K\to r_XT_XK$ induces $\iota=\sigma^{-1}Rf_{*,A}(\eta_K):M\to r_YN$. Postcomposition by $\lambda$ on $B$ induces $\tau:r_YN\to M$, and these specified maps satisfy $\tau\iota=1_M$, $\iota\tau=\rho(e)$. The scalar-adjunction transpose of $\beta_{f,K}$ is precisely $\iota$.

For every algebraically closed geometric point $y$ of $Y$, apply the exact geometric fibre functor $\Phi_{y,E}$ of [lem-sfb-constructible-normed-geometric-fibres]. Its scalar-restriction and derived tensor comparisons identify $H^q\Phi_{y,E}(r_YN)$ with the underlying $E$-space $H$ of $H^q\Phi_{y,F}(N)$ and identify the degree-$q$ source fibre with $F\otimes_E H^q\Phi_{y,E}(M)$. The $D$-action descends to $H$, and $H^q\Phi_{y,E}(\iota)$ identifies $H^q\Phi_{y,E}(M)$ with $eH$. Under these identifications the actual fibre of $\beta_{f,K}$ is $v\otimes h\mapsto\theta_vh$. All assertions are natural in $K$. There is no constructibility, boundedness, countability, completeness or coefficient-flatness assumption.

proof.text: Use the fixed internal/section equivalences. The scalar-adjunction comparison identifies exact restriction and unbounded derived extension, with their units and counits, without coefficient flatness. The geometric comparison identifies the specified derived pushpull adjunctions. Write $a_Z:A_Z\to B_Z$. The coefficient-morphisms statement gives cartesian identifications $\alpha_A:f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ and $\alpha_B:f^{-1}B_Y\cong B_X$, natural in the condensed ring. Hence $a_X\alpha_A=\alpha_Bf^{-1}(a_Y)$, exactly the compatibility required by the change-adjunction theorem. All sites are the specified small pro-etale sites, and the internal/section equivalences preserve their underlying ring sheaves. Apply the ring-sheaf change-adjunction theorem with $u=f$, $R_Z=A_Z$, $S_Z=B_Z$, and transport its comparison back to internal modules. That theorem is stated for the adjunctions $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] with $c=\alpha_A$, resp. $\alpha_B$ (in section form), while the geometric comparison lands in the canonical ringed derived pullback and K-injective direct image of the section model. These coincide: the section-model inverse image is the same tensor-formula pullback $f^{-1}(-)\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y,c}R_X$ (presheaf scalar extension then sheafification) with the same ordinary module adjunction; since $c$ is invertible it is exact, so its canonical left-derived comparison is the termwise functor on every complex; both direct images are computed on K-injective resolutions. Hence both derived adjunctions are the unique bijection of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] induced by that one ordinary adjunction. This gives the natural isomorphism $\sigma:r_YRf_{*,B}\cong Rf_{*,A}r_X$, with exactly the adjunction compatibility in that theorem. This construction uses neither a claim that restriction preserves injectives nor a flatness assumption.

proof.text: Regard $F$ and $E$ as topological $E$-modules. The inclusion $u:E\to F$, $\lambda:F\to E$, every $d\in D$, and every $m_v:F\to F$ are continuous $E$-linear maps. In particular $u\lambda=e$, $\lambda u=1$, $e^2=e$, and $m_ve=\theta_v$, by evaluating at $w\in F$ and using $\lambda(1)=1$. The continuous-module condensation functor gives internal $A$-linear maps on ALL continuous functions by postcomposition, preserving sums and composition. Apply $\operatorname{mapMod}(p_Z^*)$ to obtain $u_Z:A_Z\to r_ZB_Z$, $l_Z:r_ZB_Z\to A_Z$ and $d_Z:r_ZB_Z\to r_ZB_Z$ with the same identities. Pullback is additive because it is a left adjoint between abelian categories (finite coproducts are biproducts). The maps $d_Z$ need not be $B_Z$-linear; they will only be tensored and pushed forward in $A$-modules.

proof.text: Write $L_K=r_XT_XK$. The normalized internal scalar comparison identifies $L_K$ with $(r_XB_X)\otimes^L_{A_X}K$ (using symmetry to put the coefficient first). Thus define $a_K(d)=d_X\otimes^L1_K$ on $L_K$, $j_K=u_X\otimes^L1_K:K\to L_K$, and $t_K=l_X\otimes^L1_K:L_K\to K$, inserting the regular-module unitors. These are genuine maps in the derived category. The derived tensor normalization identifies these internal operations with the ringed derived tensor, whose additivity holds on all derived morphisms. Its bifunctor laws give $a_K(dd')=a_K(d)a_K(d')$, $a_K(1)=1$ and $a_K(d+d')=a_K(d)+a_K(d')$. The scalar-adjunction normalization computes its unit as $p\mapsto1\otimes p$ on K-flat representatives; consequently $j_K$ is the specified $\eta_K$, rather than just some split inclusion.

proof.text: Define $\rho(d)=\sigma^{-1}Rf_{*,A}(a_K(d))\sigma$. The bifunctor identities of the preceding step and functoriality give preservation of composition and identity. To justify addition after direct image, apply the ringed derived pushforward linearity theorem with the abstract ring $R=E$, using constant sections of $E$ in $A_X,A_Y$. They are central and compatible with the structural map because these coefficients are pulled from the point. Through the geometric equivalences this makes the specified internal $Rf_{*,A}$ additive and $E$-linear. Hence $\rho$ is a unital ring action. For the algebra structure and the claimed $F$-scalar compatibility, compute separately in the next step.

proof.text: On scalar-extension representatives, $a_K(m_v)$ is $b\otimes p\mapsto(vb)\otimes p$, which is exactly the underlying multiplication-by-$v$ endomorphism of $T_XK$. This representative identification is the balanced-generator normalization of internal scalar extension and tensor. Naturality of $\sigma$ for this $B_X$-linear endomorphism therefore gives $\rho(m_v)=r_YRf_{*,B}(v1_{T_XK})$. Apply ringed derived pushforward linearity with $R=F$ and the constant sections in $B_X,B_Y$, then the normalized geometric comparison: this is $v1_N$ after restriction. In particular for $a\in E$, $\rho(m_a)=a1_{r_YN}$, and $ad=m_a\circ d$ shows $\rho(ad)=a\rho(d)$. This proves that the ring action is an $E$-algebra action. No topology on $D$ or continuity of $\rho$ is asserted.

proof.text: Tensor the coefficient identities $l_Xu_X=1$ and $u_Xl_X=e_X$ with $K$. They give $t_K\eta_K=1_K$ and $\eta_Kt_K=a_K(e)$, with all unitors inserted. Set $\iota=\sigma^{-1}Rf_{*,A}(\eta_K)$ and $\tau=Rf_{*,A}(t_K)\sigma$. Applying $Rf_{*,A}$ to those two identities and cancelling adjacent $\sigma\sigma^{-1}$ gives $\tau\iota=1_M$ and $\iota\tau=\rho(e)$. Thus these are exactly the maps induced by the coefficient inclusion and the specified $\lambda$; no abstract splitting of an idempotent was chosen.

proof.text:
Put $c:f_B^*T_YM\to T_Xf_A^*M$ for the comparison used to define $\beta$, $b:r_Xf_B^*\cong f_A^*r_Y$, and $z=\sigma r_Y(\beta)\eta^Y_M$. By adjunction compatibility of $\sigma$, the geometric transpose of $z$ is
$$r_X(T_X\varepsilon_K\circ c)\,b^{-1}_{T_YM}\,f_A^*(\eta^Y_M).$$
The internal scalar-pullback normalization identifies this actual $c$ with the section-ring balanced comparison, through the same geometric adjunction identifications. By step 1 the geometric adjunctions here are those of the ring-sheaf change theorem, and its $b$, induced by the identified-coefficient inverse image, is on underlying sheaves the action identification $h_A^*r_Y=r_Xh_B^*$ of the K-flat comparison node for $h=f$, the coefficients transported along the identifications $\alpha_f$. The K-flat scalar comparison normalization identifies its inverse with the scalar mate of the restriction square and says that the balanced comparison preserves insertion of one. Therefore
$$r_X(c)\,b^{-1}_{T_YM}\,f_A^*(\eta^Y_M)=\eta^X_{f_A^*M}.$$
This is an identity of natural derived maps, not a tensor computation requiring a flat coefficient ring. Naturality of the scalar unit now makes the first displayed transpose equal to $\eta^X_K\varepsilon_K$. But the geometric transpose of $Rf_{*,A}(\eta^X_K)$ is also $\eta^X_K\varepsilon_K$, by naturality of the geometric counit and its triangle identity. The adjunction bijection gives $z=Rf_{*,A}(\eta_K)$; cancel $\sigma$ to get $r_Y(\beta)\eta^Y_M=\iota$. This is exactly the scalar-adjunction transpose of $\beta$.

proof.text: A nonarchimedean norm has clopen balls, so $E$ and $F$ have totally disconnected metric topologies. Apply the unrestricted exactness and scalar-comparison clauses of the geometric-fibre theorem at $y$; none of its Noetherian or constructibility hypotheses for the separate conservativity clause is used. They identify $\Phi_{y,E}(r_YN)$ with restricted $\Phi_{y,F}(N)$ and identify $\Phi_{y,F}(T_YM)$ with $F\otimes_E^L\Phi_{y,E}(M)$, preserving insertion of one. The abstract $E$-module $F$ is flat by the module-over-field theorem. Hence its ordinary tensor is exact, computes this derived tensor termwise, and the exact-functor/cohomology theorem gives the stated degree-$q$ source $F\otimes_EH^q\Phi_{y,E}(M)$ for every integer $q$, including unbounded $M$. This uses flatness of an abstract vector space, not flatness of $A\to B$.

proof.text: Apply $H^q\Phi_{y,E}$ to the derived maps and identities already established, and write $J$ and $T$ for the resulting $\iota$ and $\tau$. Functoriality and additivity give a $D$-action on $H$, with $TJ=1$ and $JT=e$. Thus $J$ is injective, every $Jx$ is fixed by $e$ since $eJ=JTJ=J$, and every element $eh$ equals $J(Th)$. Its image is exactly $eH$, with inverse $T$ on that image. The action of $m_v$ on $H$ is multiplication by $v$, by the scalar calculation above and the $F$-linear fibre functor.

proof.text:
Let $x\in H^q\Phi_{y,E}(M)$ and identify it with $h=Jx\in eH$. The fibre tensor comparison preserves units, and the transpose identity gives $\beta_y(1\otimes x)=Jx=h$. Since $\beta$ is a morphism of derived $B_Y$-modules its fibre is $F$-linear, whence
$$\beta_y(v\otimes x)=vJx=\rho(m_v)h=\rho(m_ve)h=\rho(\theta_v)h.$$
Here $eh=h$ and $m_ve=\theta_v$ explain the last two equalities. This proves the asserted formula for the actual specified $\beta$, not for an arbitrary isomorphism of its source and target. Every construction above is a coefficient map tensored with $1_K$, a natural comparison, or a functor applied to such a map; therefore it commutes with every morphism $K\to K'$. Empty schemes, the zero complex, and $F=E$ with $\lambda=1$ satisfy the same identities (in the last case $e=1$).
